name: Pulumi Preview

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "infrastructure/pulumi/**"
      - ".github/workflows/pulumi-preview.yml"

env:
  CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
  CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
  AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
  PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE }}
  SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_USER: PULUMI_SVC
  SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: OAUTH
  SNOWFLAKE_ROLE: PULUMI_ROLE

jobs:
  preview:
    name: Preview
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: pulumi
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: infrastructure/pulumi

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.24"
          cache-dependency-path: infrastructure/pulumi/go.sum

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: go mod tidy

      - name: Get Snowflake OIDC token
        run: |
          OIDC_TOKEN=$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
            "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=https://${SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME}-${SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME}.snowflakecomputing.com" | jq -r '.value')
          if [ -z "$OIDC_TOKEN" ] || [ "$OIDC_TOKEN" = "null" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to retrieve Snowflake OIDC token"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::add-mask::$OIDC_TOKEN"
          echo "SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN=$OIDC_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Login to R2 backend
        run: pulumi login 's3://pulumi?endpoint=https://${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com&region=auto&s3ForcePathStyle=true'

      - name: Select stack
        run: pulumi stack select dev

      - name: Pulumi Preview
        id: preview
        run: |
          set +e

          # Run preview with JSON output for parsing
          pulumi preview --json 2>/dev/null > preview.json
          JSON_EXIT=$?

          # Also get human-readable output
          pulumi preview --diff 2>&1 | tee preview.txt
          PREVIEW_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

          echo "exit_code=$PREVIEW_EXIT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Parse JSON for accurate counts
          if [ -f preview.json ] && [ -s preview.json ]; then
            CREATES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "create")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            UPDATES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "update")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            DELETES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "delete")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            SAMES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "same")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
          else
            # Fallback to text parsing
            CREATES=$(grep -c "^\s*+.*create" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            UPDATES=$(grep -c "^\s*~.*update" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            DELETES=$(grep -c "^\s*-.*delete" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            SAMES=$(grep -oP '\d+(?= unchanged)' preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
          fi

          echo "creates=$CREATES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "updates=$UPDATES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "deletes=$DELETES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "sames=$SAMES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Determine result status
          TOTAL_CHANGES=$((CREATES + UPDATES + DELETES))
          if [ $PREVIEW_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "result=failed" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          elif [ $TOTAL_CHANGES -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "result=no-changes" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "result=has-changes" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Generate PR Comment
        id: comment
        run: |
          RESULT="${{ steps.preview.outputs.result }}"
          CREATES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.creates }}"
          UPDATES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.updates }}"
          DELETES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.deletes }}"
          SAMES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.sames }}"

          # Set header based on result
          case $RESULT in
            "failed")
              HEADER="## ❌ Pulumi Preview Failed"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-failed-red?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
            "no-changes")
              HEADER="## ✅ Pulumi Preview: No Changes"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-no%20changes-green?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
            "has-changes")
              HEADER="## 🔄 Pulumi Preview: Changes Detected"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-changes%20detected-blue?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
          esac

          # Build comment
          cat << 'COMMENT_EOF' > comment.md
          HEADER_PLACEHOLDER

          ![Pulumi](BADGE_PLACEHOLDER)

          ### 📊 Resource Changes

          | | Create | Update | Delete | Unchanged |
          |:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
          | Count | **CREATES_PLACEHOLDER** | **UPDATES_PLACEHOLDER** | **DELETES_PLACEHOLDER** | SAMES_PLACEHOLDER |
          | | 🆕 | 📝 | 🗑️ | ⏸️ |

          COMMENT_EOF

          # Add warning section for destructive changes
          if [ "$DELETES" -gt 0 ]; then
            cat << 'WARNING_EOF' >> comment.md

          > [!CAUTION]
          > **DELETES_PLACEHOLDER resources will be deleted.** Please review carefully before merging.

          WARNING_EOF
          fi

          # Add details section
          cat << 'DETAILS_EOF' >> comment.md

          <details>
          <summary>📋 Preview Details</summary>

          ```diff
          DETAILS_EOF

          # Add preview output (truncated if needed)
          head -c 60000 preview.txt >> comment.md

          cat << 'END_EOF' >> comment.md
          ```

          </details>

          ---

          <sub>🏗️ **Stack:** `dev` | 📁 **Path:** `infrastructure/pulumi` | 🔗 **Workflow:** [Run #${{ github.run_number }}](${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }})</sub>
          END_EOF

          # Replace placeholders
          sed -i "s|HEADER_PLACEHOLDER|$HEADER|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|BADGE_PLACEHOLDER|$BADGE|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|CREATES_PLACEHOLDER|$CREATES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|UPDATES_PLACEHOLDER|$UPDATES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|DELETES_PLACEHOLDER|$DELETES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|SAMES_PLACEHOLDER|$SAMES|g" comment.md

      - name: Post PR Comment
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const body = fs.readFileSync('infrastructure/pulumi/comment.md', 'utf8');

            const marker = '<!-- pulumi-preview-comment -->';
            const fullBody = marker + '\n' + body;

            // Find existing comment
            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existingComment = comments.find(c => c.body.includes(marker));

            if (existingComment) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existingComment.id,
                body: fullBody
              });
              console.log('Updated existing comment');
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body: fullBody
              });
              console.log('Created new comment');
            }

      - name: Set exit code
        if: steps.preview.outputs.result == 'failed'
        run: exit 1

name: Pulumi Preview

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "infrastructure/pulumi/**"
      - ".github/workflows/pulumi-preview.yml"

env:
  CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
  CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
  AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
  PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE }}
  SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_USER: PULUMI_PREVIEW_SVC
  SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: OAUTH
  SNOWFLAKE_ROLE: PULUMI_ROLE

jobs:
  preview:
    name: Preview
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: infrastructure/pulumi

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.24"
          cache-dependency-path: infrastructure/pulumi/go.sum

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: go mod tidy

      - name: Get Snowflake OIDC token
        run: |
          OIDC_TOKEN=$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
            "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=https://${SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME}-${SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME}.snowflakecomputing.com" | jq -r '.value')
          if [ -z "$OIDC_TOKEN" ] || [ "$OIDC_TOKEN" = "null" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to retrieve Snowflake OIDC token"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::add-mask::$OIDC_TOKEN"
          echo "SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN=$OIDC_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Login to R2 backend
        run: pulumi login 's3://pulumi?endpoint=https://${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com&region=auto&s3ForcePathStyle=true'

      - name: Select stack
        run: pulumi stack select dev

      - name: Pulumi Preview
        id: preview
        run: |
          set +e

          # Run preview with JSON output for parsing
          pulumi preview --json 2>/dev/null > preview.json
          JSON_EXIT=$?

          # Also get human-readable output
          pulumi preview --diff 2>&1 | tee preview.txt
          PREVIEW_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

          echo "exit_code=$PREVIEW_EXIT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Parse JSON for accurate counts
          if [ -f preview.json ] && [ -s preview.json ]; then
            CREATES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "create")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            UPDATES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "update")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            DELETES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "delete")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            SAMES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "same")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
          else
            # Fallback to text parsing
            CREATES=$(grep -c "^\s*+.*create" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            UPDATES=$(grep -c "^\s*~.*update" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            DELETES=$(grep -c "^\s*-.*delete" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            SAMES=$(grep -oP '\d+(?= unchanged)' preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
          fi

          echo "creates=$CREATES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "updates=$UPDATES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "deletes=$DELETES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "sames=$SAMES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Determine result status
          TOTAL_CHANGES=$((CREATES + UPDATES + DELETES))
          if [ $PREVIEW_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "result=failed" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          elif [ $TOTAL_CHANGES -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "result=no-changes" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "result=has-changes" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Generate PR Comment
        id: comment
        run: |
          RESULT="${{ steps.preview.outputs.result }}"
          CREATES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.creates }}"
          UPDATES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.updates }}"
          DELETES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.deletes }}"
          SAMES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.sames }}"

          # Set header based on result
          case $RESULT in
            "failed")
              HEADER="## ❌ Pulumi Preview Failed"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-failed-red?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
            "no-changes")
              HEADER="## ✅ Pulumi Preview: No Changes"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-no%20changes-green?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
            "has-changes")
              HEADER="## 🔄 Pulumi Preview: Changes Detected"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-changes%20detected-blue?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
          esac

          # Build comment
          cat << 'COMMENT_EOF' > comment.md
          HEADER_PLACEHOLDER

          ![Pulumi](BADGE_PLACEHOLDER)

          ### 📊 Resource Changes

          | | Create | Update | Delete | Unchanged |
          |:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
          | Count | **CREATES_PLACEHOLDER** | **UPDATES_PLACEHOLDER** | **DELETES_PLACEHOLDER** | SAMES_PLACEHOLDER |
          | | 🆕 | 📝 | 🗑️ | ⏸️ |

          COMMENT_EOF

          # Add warning section for destructive changes
          if [ "$DELETES" -gt 0 ]; then
            cat << 'WARNING_EOF' >> comment.md

          > [!CAUTION]
          > **DELETES_PLACEHOLDER resources will be deleted.** Please review carefully before merging.

          WARNING_EOF
          fi

          # Add details section
          cat << 'DETAILS_EOF' >> comment.md

          <details>
          <summary>📋 Preview Details</summary>

          ```diff
          DETAILS_EOF

          # Add preview output (truncated if needed)
          head -c 60000 preview.txt >> comment.md

          cat << 'END_EOF' >> comment.md
          ```

          </details>

          ---

          <sub>🏗️ **Stack:** `dev` | 📁 **Path:** `infrastructure/pulumi` | 🔗 **Workflow:** [Run #${{ github.run_number }}](${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }})</sub>
          END_EOF

          # Replace placeholders
          sed -i "s|HEADER_PLACEHOLDER|$HEADER|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|BADGE_PLACEHOLDER|$BADGE|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|CREATES_PLACEHOLDER|$CREATES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|UPDATES_PLACEHOLDER|$UPDATES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|DELETES_PLACEHOLDER|$DELETES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|SAMES_PLACEHOLDER|$SAMES|g" comment.md

      - name: Post PR Comment
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const body = fs.readFileSync('infrastructure/pulumi/comment.md', 'utf8');

            const marker = '<!-- pulumi-preview-comment -->';
            const fullBody = marker + '\n' + body;

            // Find existing comment
            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existingComment = comments.find(c => c.body.includes(marker));

            if (existingComment) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existingComment.id,
                body: fullBody
              });
              console.log('Updated existing comment');
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body: fullBody
              });
              console.log('Created new comment');
            }

      - name: Set exit code
        if: steps.preview.outputs.result == 'failed'
        run: exit 1

考えられる原因:

1. **GitHub Environment `pulumi` が未作成** — Settings > Environments で `pulumi` という名前の environment を作成する必要があります（保護ルール不要、空でOK）。これがないと OIDC の `sub` クレームに `environment:pulumi` が含まれず、Snowflake の SUBJECT と一致しません
2. **audience の不一致** — `SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME` と `SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME` の値が Snowflake アカウント URL と一致しているか

name: Pulumi Preview

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "infrastructure/pulumi/**"
      - ".github/workflows/pulumi-preview.yml"

env:
  CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
  CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
  AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
  PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE }}
  SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_USER: PULUMI_SVC
  SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: OAUTH
  SNOWFLAKE_ROLE: PULUMI_ROLE

jobs:
  preview:
    name: Preview
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: pulumi
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: infrastructure/pulumi

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.24"
          cache-dependency-path: infrastructure/pulumi/go.sum

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: go mod tidy

      - name: Get Snowflake OIDC token
        run: |
          OIDC_TOKEN=$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
            "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=https://${SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME}-${SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME}.snowflakecomputing.com" | jq -r '.value')
          if [ -z "$OIDC_TOKEN" ] || [ "$OIDC_TOKEN" = "null" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to retrieve Snowflake OIDC token"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::add-mask::$OIDC_TOKEN"
          echo "SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN=$OIDC_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Login to R2 backend
        run: pulumi login 's3://pulumi?endpoint=https://${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com&region=auto&s3ForcePathStyle=true'

      - name: Select stack
        run: pulumi stack select dev

      - name: Pulumi Preview
        id: preview
        run: |
          set +e

          # Run preview with JSON output for parsing
          pulumi preview --json 2>/dev/null > preview.json
          JSON_EXIT=$?

          # Also get human-readable output
          pulumi preview --diff 2>&1 | tee preview.txt
          PREVIEW_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

          echo "exit_code=$PREVIEW_EXIT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Parse JSON for accurate counts
          if [ -f preview.json ] && [ -s preview.json ]; then
            CREATES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "create")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            UPDATES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "update")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            DELETES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "delete")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            SAMES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "same")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
          else
            # Fallback to text parsing
            CREATES=$(grep -c "^\s*+.*create" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            UPDATES=$(grep -c "^\s*~.*update" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            DELETES=$(grep -c "^\s*-.*delete" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            SAMES=$(grep -oP '\d+(?= unchanged)' preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
          fi

          echo "creates=$CREATES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "updates=$UPDATES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "deletes=$DELETES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "sames=$SAMES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Determine result status
          TOTAL_CHANGES=$((CREATES + UPDATES + DELETES))
          if [ $PREVIEW_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "result=failed" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          elif [ $TOTAL_CHANGES -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "result=no-changes" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "result=has-changes" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Generate PR Comment
        id: comment
        run: |
          RESULT="${{ steps.preview.outputs.result }}"
          CREATES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.creates }}"
          UPDATES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.updates }}"
          DELETES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.deletes }}"
          SAMES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.sames }}"

          # Set header based on result
          case $RESULT in
            "failed")
              HEADER="## ❌ Pulumi Preview Failed"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-failed-red?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
            "no-changes")
              HEADER="## ✅ Pulumi Preview: No Changes"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-no%20changes-green?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
            "has-changes")
              HEADER="## 🔄 Pulumi Preview: Changes Detected"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-changes%20detected-blue?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
          esac

          # Build comment
          cat << 'COMMENT_EOF' > comment.md
          HEADER_PLACEHOLDER

          ![Pulumi](BADGE_PLACEHOLDER)

          ### 📊 Resource Changes

          | | Create | Update | Delete | Unchanged |
          |:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
          | Count | **CREATES_PLACEHOLDER** | **UPDATES_PLACEHOLDER** | **DELETES_PLACEHOLDER** | SAMES_PLACEHOLDER |
          | | 🆕 | 📝 | 🗑️ | ⏸️ |

          COMMENT_EOF

          # Add warning section for destructive changes
          if [ "$DELETES" -gt 0 ]; then
            cat << 'WARNING_EOF' >> comment.md

          > [!CAUTION]
          > **DELETES_PLACEHOLDER resources will be deleted.** Please review carefully before merging.

          WARNING_EOF
          fi

          # Add details section
          cat << 'DETAILS_EOF' >> comment.md

          <details>
          <summary>📋 Preview Details</summary>

          ```diff
          DETAILS_EOF

          # Add preview output (truncated if needed)
          head -c 60000 preview.txt >> comment.md

          cat << 'END_EOF' >> comment.md
          ```

          </details>

          ---

          <sub>🏗️ **Stack:** `dev` | 📁 **Path:** `infrastructure/pulumi` | 🔗 **Workflow:** [Run #${{ github.run_number }}](${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }})</sub>
          END_EOF

          # Replace placeholders
          sed -i "s|HEADER_PLACEHOLDER|$HEADER|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|BADGE_PLACEHOLDER|$BADGE|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|CREATES_PLACEHOLDER|$CREATES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|UPDATES_PLACEHOLDER|$UPDATES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|DELETES_PLACEHOLDER|$DELETES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|SAMES_PLACEHOLDER|$SAMES|g" comment.md

      - name: Post PR Comment
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const body = fs.readFileSync('infrastructure/pulumi/comment.md', 'utf8');

            const marker = '<!-- pulumi-preview-comment -->';
            const fullBody = marker + '\n' + body;

            // Find existing comment
            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existingComment = comments.find(c => c.body.includes(marker));

            if (existingComment) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existingComment.id,
                body: fullBody
              });
              console.log('Updated existing comment');
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body: fullBody
              });
              console.log('Created new comment');
            }

      - name: Set exit code
        if: steps.preview.outputs.result == 'failed'
        run: exit 1

Based on the web search results, here's what I found about Snowflake Workload Identity Federation, GitHub Actions, and OIDC authentication:

## Key Overview

Snowflake released Workload Identity Federation (WIF) in August 2025, enabling secure, secretless authentication for applications and services. Workload identity federation is a service-to-service authentication method that lets workloads, such as applications, services, or containers, authenticate with Snowflake using their cloud provider's native identity system, such as AWS Identity and Access Management (AWS IAM) roles, Microsoft Entra ID, and Google Cloud service accounts to get an attestation that Snowflake can use and validate.

## How It Works with GitHub Actions

With OIDC, GitHub Actions requests a short-lived token at runtime. Snowflake validates this token against the issuer (GitHub), and if the claims match, authentication succeeds. No secrets to leak, rotate or manage.

The snow auth oidc commands enable secure, password-less authentication to Snowflake. It leverages OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens from CI/CD environments like GitHub Actions. This feature supports workload identity federation (WIF), enabling automated systems to access Snowflake without static credentials, which aligns with security best practices.

## Setup Configuration

To set up WIF OIDC with GitHub Actions, you need to:

1. Create a service user with the OIDC workload identity type using CREATE USER with TYPE = SERVICE and WORKLOAD_IDENTITY configuration specifying the GitHub OIDC issuer and subject.

2. The id-token: write permission is required for GitHub to issue the OIDC token, and the environment must match the subject claim you configured in Snowflake.

## Benefits

With Workload Identity Federation, you've eliminated long-lived credentials from your CI/CD pipeline. No more rotating keys, no more secrets sprawl. You now have a more secure, auditable, ephemeral authentication.

Based on the search results, here's a comparison of WORKLOAD_IDENTITY vs OAUTH authentication methods in the gosnowflake driver:

## WORKLOAD_IDENTITY

To authenticate via workload identity, specify workload_identity, which requires the workloadIdentityProvider option to be set (AWS, GCP, AZURE, OIDC). This method enables applications, services, or containers to authenticate with Snowflake by leveraging their cloud provider's native identity system, such as AWS IAM, Microsoft Entra ID, or Google Cloud service accounts.

Key benefits of WORKLOAD_IDENTITY:
- Removes the need to manage and store long-lived credentials such as passwords, API keys, key pairs, and programmatic access tokens for authenticating to Snowflake
- Eliminates the need for managing long-lived credentials and simplifies credential acquisition compared to other methods like External OAuth

## OAUTH

To authenticate via OAuth, specify oauth and provide an OAuth Access Token. The gosnowflake driver also supports OAuth2 authorization code and client credential flows.

## Key Differences

Workload identity federation reduces the complexity involved in getting credentials, where other methods, such as External OAuth can require more effort to set up. In essence, WORKLOAD_IDENTITY is designed for service-to-service authentication using cloud provider native identities, while OAUTH is better suited for scenarios requiring OAuth tokens or authorization flows.

## Key Findings

The Snowflake Go driver has added support for workload identity federation in the AWS, Azure, GCP, and Kubernetes platforms. 

**Accessing the Feature:**
This feature can only be accessed by setting the SF_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTHENTICATION environment variable to true. However, you should use this feature only with non-production data.

**Connection Parameters:**
The Go driver has added the WorkloadIdentityProvider connection parameter and AuthTypeWorkloadIdentityFederation to the values for the authenticator connection parameter.

**OIDC Token Support:**
The feature allows workloads to use OIDC tokens from their respective platforms. Snowflake accepts ID tokens generated by the IdP as proof of the workload's identity.

```sql
  )

```

# Workload Identity Federation in Go Snowflake Driver

## Version and Status

**Version 1.16.0** (August 14, 2025) introduced full support for workload identity federation as a generally available feature. However, it was initially offered as a Private Preview feature in Version 1.15.0 (July 1, 2025).

## Supported Platforms

The feature works across multiple cloud environments: "AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Kubernetes platforms."

## Configuration Details

**Authenticator Parameter:** `AuthTypeWorkloadIdentityFederation` is the value to use for the authenticator connection parameter.

**Connection Parameter:** A new `WorkloadIdentityProvider` connection parameter was introduced to configure this authentication method.

## Experimental Access (Earlier Versions)

For versions 1.15.0 and earlier that offered this as Private Preview, the feature required setting the `SF_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTHENTICATION` environment variable to `true`. This restriction was lifted when the feature achieved general availability in version 1.16.0.

# Snowflake OIDC with GitHub Actions Setup Guide

## Authentication Method
The guide uses **OIDC (OpenID Connect)** with GitHub Actions—no traditional passwords or key pairs required. "GitHub Actions requests a short-lived token at runtime. Snowflake validates this token against the issuer (GitHub)."

## Three Core Steps

### Step 1: Create a Least-Privilege Role
Define environment-scoped roles before setting up service users:
```sql
CREATE ROLE TEST_CICD_ROLE;
GRANT CREATE SCHEMA ON DATABASE TEST_DATABASE TO ROLE TEST_CICD_ROLE;
```

### Step 2: Create a Service User with Workload Identity
The critical configuration ties the user to your GitHub repository and environment:
```sql
CREATE USER TEST_SVC_INFRA_GITHUB
	DEFAULT_ROLE = TEST_CICD_ROLE
	TYPE = SERVICE
	WORKLOAD_IDENTITY = (
	 TYPE = OIDC
	 ISSUER = 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com'
	 SUBJECT = 'repo:MechRock/snowflake-infrastructure:environment:test'
);
GRANT ROLE TEST_CICD_ROLE TO USER TEST_SVC_INFRA_GITHUB;
```

**Critical Detail:** The SUBJECT claim is case-sensitive and must match your organization, repository, and GitHub environment exactly.

### Step 3: Configure GitHub Actions Workflow
```yaml
name: Snowflake OIDC
on: workflow_dispatch

permissions:
 id-token: write
 contents: read

jobs:
 oidc-job:
   runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   environment: test
   steps:
     - name: Set up Snowflake CLI
       uses: snowflakedb/snowflake-cli-action@v2.0
       with:
         use-oidc: true
         cli-version: "3.14.0"
     - name: test connection
       env:
         SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT: A1234567890-MECHROCK
       run: snow connection test -x
```

## Required Environment Variables
- **SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT**: Your Snowflake account identifier

## Security Notes
- No security integration object is explicitly mentioned as needed
- The `id-token: write` permission is mandatory for GitHub to issue tokens
- The `environment: test` setting must match your SUBJECT claim configuration

# Snowflake Provider Authentication Options

## WORKLOAD_IDENTITY Support

Yes, the Snowflake provider supports the `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` authenticator. According to the documentation, valid authentication options include: `"SNOWFLAKE | OAUTH | EXTERNALBROWSER | OKTA | SNOWFLAKE_JWT | TOKENACCESSOR | USERNAMEPASSWORDMFA | PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN | OAUTH_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS | OAUTH_AUTHORIZATION_CODE | WORKLOAD_IDENTITY"`

## Version Information

The documentation shown is for **Snowflake v2.12.0, published February 13, 2026**. No specific version history for when workload identity support was introduced is provided in this content.

## Related Configuration Options

The provider includes two workload identity-specific parameters:

1. **WorkloadIdentityProvider** - `"The workload identity provider to use for WIF authentication."` Sourced from `SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` environment variable.

2. **WorkloadIdentityEntraResource** - `"The resource to use for WIF authentication on Azure environment."` Sourced from `SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_ENTRA_RESOURCE` environment variable.

## Token Configuration

The provider also supports general token-based authentication through the `token` parameter and `SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN` environment variable, with automatic authenticator adjustment when configured.

# GitHub Actions OIDC Integration with Snowflake CLI

## Overview
The integration uses the official `snowflakedb/snowflake-cli-action@v2.0` GitHub Action to automate Snowflake workflows within CI/CD pipelines.

## Environment Variables Required

For OIDC authentication, you need:
- **`SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`**: Your Snowflake account identifier (stored as a GitHub secret)

That's the primary requirement. The OIDC token is automatically generated by GitHub Actions when properly configured.

## Connection Configuration

### Step 1: Create a Service User
```sql
CREATE USER <username>
TYPE = SERVICE
WORKLOAD_IDENTITY = (
  TYPE = OIDC
  ISSUER = 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com'
  SUBJECT = '<your_subject>'
)
```

The subject typically follows the pattern: `"repo:<owner/repo>:environment:<env_name>"`

### Step 2: Workflow YAML Setup

```yaml
name: Snowflake OIDC
on: [push]

permissions:
  id-token: write    # Required for OIDC token generation
  contents: read

jobs:
  oidc-job:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: test-env  # Must match environment in subject
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      
      - name: Set up Snowflake CLI
        uses: snowflakedb/snowflake-cli-action@v2.0
        with:
          use-oidc: true
          cli-version: "3.11"
      
      - name: test connection
        env:
          SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT }}
        run: snow connection test -x
```

## Direct Tool Usage
The integration uses **Snowflake CLI directly**, not a driver. Commands are executed via the `snow` command-line tool (e.g., `snow connection test -x`, `snow notebook create`).

# Workload Identity Federation in Go Snowflake Driver

## Overview

Workload Identity Federation allows authentication via workload identity instead of traditional credentials. It supports multiple identity providers.

## Authenticator Constant

```go
AuthTypeWorkloadIdentityFederation
```

## Supported Providers

Set via the `WorkloadIdentityProvider` field:
- **AWS**
- **GCP**
- **AZURE**
- **OIDC**

## Required Config Fields

```go
type Config struct {
    Authenticator              AuthType  // Set to AuthTypeWorkloadIdentityFederation
    WorkloadIdentityProvider   string    // "AWS", "GCP", "AZURE", or "OIDC"
    WorkloadIdentityImpersonationPath string // Optional, comma-separated list
}
```

## Provider-Specific Configuration

### AWS
- `WorkloadIdentityImpersonationPath`: Comma-separated list of role ARNs to assume

### GCP
- `WorkloadIdentityImpersonationPath`: Comma-separated list where the last parameter is the target service account and the rest are chained delegation

### AZURE
- `WorkloadIdentityEntraResource`: Optional, customize Entra resource for JWT token fetching

### OIDC
- Requires appropriate OIDC token provisioning

## OIDC Token Handling

The OIDC token is obtained from the environment/system's workload identity provider. The driver automatically:
1. Retrieves the token from the workload identity provider
2. Exchanges it for a Snowflake session token
3. Uses it for authentication

You do not manually pass the OIDC token—the driver handles token exchange internally when using workload identity federation.

## DSN Example

```
authenticator=workload_identity&workload_identity_provider=GCP&workload_identity_impersonation_path=sa1,sa2,target-sa
```

## References

For complete details, refer to: [Snowflake Workload Identity Federation Documentation](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/workload-identity-federation)

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about how OIDC tokens are obtained in GitHub Actions workflows:

## How the Driver Gets the Token via `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL`

In GitHub Actions, you can use the environment variables `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` to request an ID token for your workflow.

The process for using gosnowflake with OIDC workload identity works as follows:

1. **GitHub Actions provides the environment variables**: To enable requesting an OIDC token, you need to set `id-token` to `write` under permissions in your GitHub Actions workflow.

2. **Driver usage**: You can configure your workload to use any Snowflake driver that supports workload identity federation. The gosnowflake driver supports this authentication method.

3. **Token exchange**: With OIDC, GitHub Actions requests a short-lived token at runtime. Snowflake validates this token against the issuer (GitHub), and if the claims match, authentication succeeds.

For GitHub Actions specifically, the OIDC issuer is configured as `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`, which matches the GitHub Actions OIDC provider.

The gosnowflake driver internally handles the token retrieval by reading the `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` environment variables provided by GitHub Actions during workflow execution, allowing it to obtain the JWT token needed for Snowflake authentication.

## Key Findings

**WIF OIDC Authentication Overview:**
WIF OIDC authentication provides a secure and modern way to authenticate with Snowflake without storing private keys as secrets, using GitHub's OIDC (OpenID Connect) token to authenticate with Snowflake.

**GitHub Actions Support:**
Snowflake released Workload Identity Federation (WIF) in August 2025, enabling secure, secretless authentication for applications and services. The snow auth OIDC commands are currently limited to GitHub Actions as the provider.

**Token Retrieval:**
With OIDC, GitHub Actions requests a short-lived token at runtime, and Snowflake validates this token against the issuer (GitHub).

**Service User Configuration:**
To set up WIF OIDC authentication, create a service user with the OIDC workload identity type using the issuer 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com' and your subject claim.

**Driver Support:**
You can configure your workload to use any Snowflake driver that supports workload identity federation.

The search results confirm that Snowflake's WIF supports OIDC with GitHub Actions, though the documentation doesn't specifically highlight "custom OIDC" providers beyond the official GitHub Actions OIDC provider at this time.

# Workload Identity Federation in gosnowflake

## Authenticator Type Constants

The code defines several authentication types, including:

```go
const (
    AuthTypeWorkloadIdentityFederation AuthType = iota + 10
    // ... other types
)
```

The `String()` method returns `"WORKLOAD_IDENTITY"` for this authenticator type.

## OIDC Token Retrieval

In the `createRequestBody` function, workload identity federation authentication is handled as follows:

```go
case AuthTypeWorkloadIdentityFederation:
    logger.WithContext(sc.ctx).Debug("Workload Identity Federation")
    wifAttestationProvider := createWifAttestationProvider(sc.ctx, sc.cfg, sc.telemetry)
    wifAttestation, err := wifAttestationProvider.getAttestation(sc.cfg.WorkloadIdentityProvider)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    if wifAttestation == nil {
        return nil, errors.New("workload identity federation attestation is not available")
    }
    requestMain.Authenticator = AuthTypeWorkloadIdentityFederation.String()
    requestMain.Token = wifAttestation.Credential
    requestMain.Provider = wifAttestation.ProviderType
```

**Key observations:**
- The driver uses a `wifAttestationProvider` to obtain attestation
- It calls `getAttestation()` with the configured `WorkloadIdentityProvider`
- The credential and provider type are extracted from the attestation response

The actual OIDC token retrieval mechanism (including potential `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` environment variable handling) would be implemented in the `createWifAttestationProvider` function, which is not shown in this code excerpt.

Based on the search results, here's information about Snowflake OIDC workload identity with the `OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST` parameter and GitHub Actions configuration:

## OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST Configuration

The `OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST` parameter is used when creating a Snowflake service user with OIDC workload identity, typically set to `('snowflakecomputing.com')`.

## Service User Setup with GitHub Actions

When creating a service user for GitHub Actions authentication, you define the workload identity with the GitHub OIDC issuer, a specific subject claim restricting to repositories and branches, and the OIDC audience list:

```sql
CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS GHA_WIF_USER TYPE = SERVICE 
WORKLOAD_IDENTITY = ( 
  TYPE = OIDC, 
  ISSUER = 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com', 
  SUBJECT = 'repo:<OWNER>/<REPO_NAME>:ref:refs/heads/main', 
  OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST = ('snowflakecomputing.com') 
);
```

## GitHub Actions Workflow Integration

In your GitHub Actions workflow, you can retrieve the OIDC token using the `actions/github-script` action with the audience parameter set to 'snowflakecomputing.com', then use that token to authenticate with Snowflake using the Snowflake connector.

This approach enables secure authentication without using passwords or private keys by defining the workload identity to authenticate as a service user.

Based on the search results, here's how OIDC tokens are obtained in Snowflake workload identity federation:

## Token Obtainment Methods

When using workload identity federation with OIDC, you can specify a token file path parameter in the Snowflake connector connection configuration. There are two primary ways to obtain and provide OIDC tokens:

### 1. From a Token File

The `token_file_path` parameter specifies the path to a service account token that was created during configuration. For example, with EKS, the token path would be /var/run/secrets/tokens/snowflake-token.

### 2. From CI/CD Environments (GitHub Actions)

Snowflake OIDC leverages OpenID Connect tokens from CI/CD environments like GitHub Actions, using workload identity federation to enable automated systems to access Snowflake without static credentials.

In GitHub Actions specifically, GitHub Actions requests a short-lived token at runtime, and Snowflake validates this token against the issuer (GitHub), with authentication succeeding if the claims match.

The `use-oidc: true` flag in GitHub Actions configuration enables OIDC authentication, where the action configures the CLI to use GitHub's OIDC token for authentication with Snowflake.

### Token as Direct String

You can also pass the JWT token directly as a string to the `token` parameter in the Snowflake connector, as an alternative to using `token_file_path`.

## Snowflake Workload Identity and OIDC

Snowflake released Workload Identity Federation (WIF) in August 2025, enabling secure, secretless authentication for applications and services.

## Snowflake Terraform Provider Support

The Snowflake Terraform provider adds comprehensive workload identity federation support to the snowflake_user resource, enabling authentication via AWS IAM, Azure, GCP, and OIDC identity providers. The workload_identity schema supports issuer (required for Azure/OIDC) and subject (required for Azure/GCP/OIDC), with an optional oidc_audience_list for OIDC.

## GitHub Actions Integration with Snowflake OIDC

For GitHub Actions integration, the id-token: write permission is required for GitHub to issue the OIDC token, and the environment must match the subject claim you configured in Snowflake.

The basic Snowflake user creation with OIDC involves: defining a user with WORKLOAD_IDENTITY including TYPE = OIDC, ISSUER = 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com', and SUBJECT matching your repository environment.

The Snowflake CLI snow auth oidc commands are currently limited to GitHub Actions as the provider.

The search results show working examples with the Snowflake CLI and broader architectural patterns for OIDC authentication across platforms, though specific Terraform provider environment variable configurations for 2025 may require consulting the official Snowflake Terraform provider documentation directly.

1→name: Pulumi Deploy
     2→
     3→on:
     4→  push:
     5→    branches: [main]
     6→    paths:
     7→      - "infrastructure/pulumi/**"
     8→      - ".github/workflows/pulumi-deploy.yml"
     9→
    10→env:
    11→  CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
    12→  CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
    13→  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
    14→  AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
    15→  PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE }}
    16→  SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME }}
    17→  SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
    18→  SNOWFLAKE_USER: PULUMI_SVC
    19→  SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: OAUTH
    20→  SNOWFLAKE_ROLE: PULUMI_ROLE
    21→
    22→jobs:
    23→  deploy:
    24→    name: Deploy
    25→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    26→    environment: pulumi
    27→    permissions:
    28→      id-token: write
    29→      contents: read
    30→    defaults:
    31→      run:
    32→        working-directory: infrastructure/pulumi
    33→
    34→    steps:
    35→      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    36→
    37→      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
    38→        with:
    39→          go-version: "1.24"
    40→          cache-dependency-path: infrastructure/pulumi/go.sum
    41→
    42→      - name: Install dependencies
    43→        run: go mod tidy
    44→
    45→      - name: Get Snowflake OIDC token
    46→        run: |
    47→          OIDC_TOKEN=$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
    48→            "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=https://${SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME}-${SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME}.snowflakecomputing.com" | jq -r '.value')
    49→          if [ -z "$OIDC_TOKEN" ] || [ "$OIDC_TOKEN" = "null" ]; then
    50→            echo "::error::Failed to retrieve Snowflake OIDC token"
    51→            exit 1
    52→          fi
    53→          echo "::add-mask::$OIDC_TOKEN"
    54→          echo "SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN=$OIDC_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    55→
    56→      - name: Login to R2 backend
    57→        run: pulumi login 's3://pulumi?endpoint=https://${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com&region=auto&s3ForcePathStyle=true'
    58→
    59→      - name: Select stack
    60→        run: pulumi stack select dev
    61→
    62→      - name: Pulumi Up
    63→        run: pulumi up --yes --refresh
    64→

---

## Research Results: Snowflake Workload Identity Federation (WIF) with GitHub Actions OIDC

### Root Cause of Your Error

**The error `390303 (08004): Invalid OAuth access token` is occurring because you are using `SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR=OAUTH` when you should be using `SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR=WORKLOAD_IDENTITY`.** This is the core issue. The `OAUTH` authenticator expects a token obtained through an External OAuth security integration flow, not a raw OIDC JWT from GitHub Actions. The `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` authenticator is specifically designed for WIF/OIDC authentication.

---

### 1. Does the gosnowflake driver support WIF/OIDC auth? What version is needed?

**Yes.** The Go Snowflake driver (`gosnowflake`) supports Workload Identity Federation:

- **v1.15.0** (July 1, 2025): Added as **Private Preview** (PrPr). Required setting `SF_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTHENTICATION=true`.
- **v1.16.0** (August 14, 2025): Promoted to **General Availability (GA)**. The experimental flag is no longer required.

The driver added:
- `AuthTypeWorkloadIdentityFederation` authenticator constant (string value: `"WORKLOAD_IDENTITY"`)
- `WorkloadIdentityProvider` connection parameter (accepts `"AWS"`, `"GCP"`, `"AZURE"`, or `"OIDC"`)

**Your problem:** The Pulumi Snowflake provider v2.12.0 (from your `go.mod`: `github.com/pulumi/pulumi-snowflake/sdk/v2 v2.12.0`) wraps the Terraform Snowflake provider. The Pulumi provider v2.12.0 **does** list `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` as a valid authenticator value per the [Pulumi Registry docs](https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/snowflake/api-docs/provider/). However, the key question is whether the underlying gosnowflake version bundled with this provider is >= v1.16.0. Since the Pulumi provider v2.12.0 was published on February 13, 2025, which is **before** gosnowflake v1.15.0 (July 2025), there is a timeline mismatch.

**Important caveat:** The Pulumi Snowflake provider SDK (`pulumi-snowflake/sdk/v2`) is the SDK for declaring resources, not the runtime driver. The actual Snowflake connection is made by the Pulumi *provider binary* (downloaded at runtime), which has its own gosnowflake dependency. The provider binary version may be newer than the SDK version. You should check which provider plugin version Pulumi is actually downloading.

---

### 2. Does `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY (TYPE = OIDC)` on a user work with `authenticator=OAUTH`?

**No.** This is the fundamental mismatch causing your error.

- **`authenticator=OAUTH`**: Expects an OAuth access token obtained through Snowflake's **External OAuth** security integration. The token must be issued by an OAuth authorization server that Snowflake trusts via a configured security integration.
- **`authenticator=WORKLOAD_IDENTITY`**: This is the correct authenticator for WIF. When combined with `workloadIdentityProvider=OIDC`, the driver handles OIDC token retrieval and exchange with Snowflake directly.

Your current workflow at `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/.github/workflows/pulumi-deploy.yml` (line 19) sets:
```yaml
SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: OAUTH
```

This needs to be changed to:
```yaml
SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: WORKLOAD_IDENTITY
```

And you also need to add:
```yaml
SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER: OIDC
```

---

### 3. Do we also need a Snowflake Security Integration (EXTERNAL_OAUTH)?

**No.** Workload Identity Federation does **not** require an `EXTERNAL_OAUTH` security integration. The `EXTERNAL_OAUTH` security integration is only needed for the traditional OAuth flow (when using `authenticator=OAUTH`).

With WIF, the trust relationship is established directly on the **user object** via the `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` parameter:

```sql
CREATE USER PULUMI_SVC
  TYPE = SERVICE
  DEFAULT_ROLE = PULUMI_ROLE
  WORKLOAD_IDENTITY = (
    TYPE = OIDC
    ISSUER = 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com'
    SUBJECT = 'repo:ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare:environment:pulumi'
    OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST = ('snowflakecomputing.com')
  );
```

Snowflake validates the OIDC JWT directly against the issuer's JWKS endpoint -- no intermediary security integration is needed.

---

### 4. Is there a known issue with the Pulumi Snowflake provider (v2.12.0) and WIF auth?

The Pulumi Snowflake provider v2.12.0 documentation [lists `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` as a valid authenticator](https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/snowflake/api-docs/provider/), along with the `workloadIdentityProvider` configuration parameter (sourced from `SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` env var).

However, there is a potential issue: the **WIF feature in gosnowflake only reached GA in v1.16.0 (August 14, 2025)**. The Pulumi provider v2.12.0 published Feb 13, 2025, may be using an older gosnowflake version that predates WIF support entirely. If the actual provider plugin binary bundled with Pulumi is from before August 2025, WIF may not work even if the configuration accepts the value.

**Recommendation:** Check which version of the provider plugin Pulumi is actually running. You can see this with `pulumi plugin ls`. If the provider plugin binary uses gosnowflake < v1.15.0, you will need to upgrade it.

---

### 5. What is the correct way to authenticate from GitHub Actions to Snowflake using OIDC?

There are **two approaches**:

#### Approach A: Using Snowflake CLI (Recommended/Simplest)

The [Snowflake CLI action](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-cli-action) has built-in OIDC support:

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: pulumi
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Snowflake CLI
        uses: snowflakedb/snowflake-cli-action@v2.0
        with:
          use-oidc: true
          cli-version: "3.14.0"
      - name: Test connection
        env:
          SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT }}
        run: snow connection test -x
```

This approach lets the Snowflake CLI handle all token retrieval and exchange internally.

#### Approach B: Using the Driver Directly (Your Use Case with Pulumi)

For the Pulumi provider, you need to configure the environment variables correctly. The driver (when using `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` authenticator with `OIDC` provider) will automatically read the `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` environment variables provided by GitHub Actions to obtain the OIDC token. **You may not need to manually fetch the token at all.**

However, you can also pass the token explicitly. Here is the corrected workflow:

```yaml
env:
  SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_USER: PULUMI_SVC
  SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: WORKLOAD_IDENTITY
  SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER: OIDC
  SNOWFLAKE_ROLE: PULUMI_ROLE

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: pulumi
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
```

If the driver handles token retrieval automatically (which it should for GitHub Actions when `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` are available), you can remove the manual OIDC token fetch step entirely. If it does not, you can pass the token via `SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN`.

#### Snowflake User Configuration

The `OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST` parameter is important. When you manually request a token with a custom audience like `https://ORG-ACCOUNT.snowflakecomputing.com`, the user must be configured to accept that audience. Alternatively, use the standard audience `snowflakecomputing.com`:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE USER PULUMI_SVC
  TYPE = SERVICE
  DEFAULT_ROLE = PULUMI_ROLE
  WORKLOAD_IDENTITY = (
    TYPE = OIDC
    ISSUER = 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com'
    SUBJECT = 'repo:ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare:environment:pulumi'
    OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST = ('snowflakecomputing.com')
  );
GRANT ROLE PULUMI_ROLE TO USER PULUMI_SVC;
```

And in the workflow, request the token with `audience=snowflakecomputing.com` if you must fetch it manually:
```yaml
- name: Get Snowflake OIDC token
  run: |
    OIDC_TOKEN=$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
      "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=snowflakecomputing.com" | jq -r '.value')
    echo "::add-mask::$OIDC_TOKEN"
    echo "SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN=$OIDC_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
```

---

### Summary of Required Changes

| What | Current (Broken) | Correct |
|------|-----------------|---------|
| Authenticator | `SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR=OAUTH` | `SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR=WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` |
| WIF Provider | (not set) | `SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER=OIDC` |
| Security Integration | Not needed | Not needed (confirmed) |
| Manual token fetch | May not be needed | Driver may auto-retrieve via `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` |
| gosnowflake version | Must be >= v1.15.0 (PrPr) or >= v1.16.0 (GA) | Check with `pulumi plugin ls` |
| User OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST | Verify it matches the `audience` in your token request | Must match |

- `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/.github/workflows/pulumi-deploy.yml` (line 19)

to:
```yaml

SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER: OIDC
```

- **v1.16.0** (August 14, 2025): Promoted to **General Availability (GA)**. The experimental flag is no longer required.

The driver added:
- `AuthTypeWorkloadIdentityFederation` authenticator constant (string value: `"WORKLOAD_IDENTITY"`)
- `WorkloadIdentityProvider` connection parameter (accepts `"AWS"`, `"GCP"`, `"AZURE"`, or `"OIDC"`)

**Your problem:** The Pulumi Snowflake provider v2.12.0 (from your `go.mod`: `github.com/pulumi/pulumi-snowflake/sdk/v2 v2.12.0`) wraps the Terraform Snowflake provider. The Pulumi provider v2.12.0 **does** list `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` as a valid authenticator value per the [Pulumi Registry docs](https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/snowflake/api-docs/provider/). However, the key question is whether the underlying gosnowflake version bundled with this provider is >= v1.16.0. Since the Pulumi provider v2.12.0 was published on February 13, 2025, which is **before** gosnowflake v1.15.0 (July 2025), there is a timeline mismatch.

**Important caveat:** The Pulumi Snowflake provider SDK (`pulumi-snowflake/sdk/v2`) is the SDK for declaring resources, not the runtime driver. The actual Snowflake connection is made by the Pulumi *provider binary* (downloaded at runtime), which has its own gosnowflake dependency. The provider binary version may be newer than the SDK version. You should check which provider plugin version Pulumi is actually downloading.

---

### 2. Does `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY (TYPE = OIDC)` on a user work with `authenticator=OAUTH`?

**No.** This is the fundamental mismatch causing your error.

- **`authenticator=OAUTH`**: Expects an OAuth access token obtained through Snowflake's **External OAuth** security integration. The token must be issued by an OAuth authorization server that Snowflake trusts via a configured security integration.
- **`authenticator=WORKLOAD_IDENTITY`**: This is the correct authenticator for WIF. When combined with `workloadIdentityProvider=OIDC`, the driver handles OIDC token retrieval and exchange with Snowflake directly.

Your current workflow at `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/.github/workflows/pulumi-deploy.yml` (line 19) sets:
```yaml
SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: OAUTH
```

This needs to be changed to:
```yaml
SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: WORKLOAD_IDENTITY
```

And you also need to add:
```yaml
SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER: OIDC
```

---

### 3. Do we also need a Snowflake Security Integration (EXTERNAL_OAUTH)?

**No.** Workload Identity Federation does **not** require an `EXTERNAL_OAUTH` security integration. The `EXTERNAL_OAUTH` security integration is only needed for the traditional OAuth flow (when using `authenticator=OAUTH`).

With WIF, the trust relationship is established directly on the **user object** via the `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` parameter:

```sql
CREATE USER PULUMI_SVC
  TYPE = SERVICE
  DEFAULT_ROLE = PULUMI_ROLE
  WORKLOAD_IDENTITY = (
    TYPE = OIDC
    ISSUER = 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com'
    SUBJECT = 'repo:ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare:environment:pulumi'
    OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST = ('snowflakecomputing.com')
  );
```

Snowflake validates the OIDC JWT directly against the issuer's JWKS endpoint -- no intermediary security integration is needed.

---

### 4. Is there a known issue with the Pulumi Snowflake provider (v2.12.0) and WIF auth?

The Pulumi Snowflake provider v2.12.0 documentation [lists `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` as a valid authenticator](https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/snowflake/api-docs/provider/), along with the `workloadIdentityProvider` configuration parameter (sourced from `SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` env var).

However, there is a potential issue: the **WIF feature in gosnowflake only reached GA in v1.16.0 (August 14, 2025)**. The Pulumi provider v2.12.0 published Feb 13, 2025, may be using an older gosnowflake version that predates WIF support entirely. If the actual provider plugin binary bundled with Pulumi is from before August 2025, WIF may not work even if the configuration accepts the value.

**Recommendation:** Check which version of the provider plugin Pulumi is actually running. You can see this with `pulumi plugin ls`. If the provider plugin binary uses gosnowflake < v1.15.0, you will need to upgrade it.

---

### 5. What is the correct way to authenticate from GitHub Actions to Snowflake using OIDC?

There are **two approaches**:

#### Approach A: Using Snowflake CLI (Recommended/Simplest)

The [Snowflake CLI action](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-cli-action) has built-in OIDC support:

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: pulumi
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Snowflake CLI
        uses: snowflakedb/snowflake-cli-action@v2.0
        with:
          use-oidc: true
          cli-version: "3.14.0"
      - name: Test connection
        env:
          SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT }}
        run: snow connection test -x
```

This approach lets the Snowflake CLI handle all token retrieval and exchange internally.

#### Approach B: Using the Driver Directly (Your Use Case with Pulumi)

For the Pulumi provider, you need to configure the environment variables correctly. The driver (when using `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` authenticator with `OIDC` provider) will automatically read the `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` environment variables provided by GitHub Actions to obtain the OIDC token. **You may not need to manually fetch the token at all.**

However, you can also pass the token explicitly. Here is the corrected workflow:

```yaml
env:
  SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_USER: PULUMI_SVC
  SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: WORKLOAD_IDENTITY
  SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER: OIDC
  SNOWFLAKE_ROLE: PULUMI_ROLE

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: pulumi
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
```

If the driver handles token retrieval automatically (which it should for GitHub Actions when `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` are available), you can remove the manual OIDC token fetch step entirely. If it does not, you can pass the token via `SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN`.

#### Snowflake User Configuration

The `OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST` parameter is important. When you manually request a token with a custom audience like `https://ORG-ACCOUNT.snowflakecomputing.com`, the user must be configured to accept that audience. Alternatively, use the standard audience `snowflakecomputing.com`:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE USER PULUMI_SVC
  TYPE = SERVICE
  DEFAULT_ROLE = PULUMI_ROLE
  WORKLOAD_IDENTITY = (
    TYPE = OIDC
    ISSUER = 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com'
    SUBJECT = 'repo:ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare:environment:pulumi'
    OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST = ('snowflakecomputing.com')
  );
GRANT ROLE PULUMI_ROLE TO USER PULUMI_SVC;
```

And in the workflow, request the token with `audience=snowflakecomputing.com` if you must fetch it manually:
```yaml
- name: Get Snowflake OIDC token
  run: |
    OIDC_TOKEN=$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
      "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=snowflakecomputing.com" | jq -r '.value')
    echo "::add-mask::$OIDC_TOKEN"
    echo "SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN=$OIDC_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
```

jobs:

        with:

          cache-dependency-path: infrastructure/pulumi/go.sum

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: go mod tidy

      - name: Get Snowflake OIDC token
        run: |
          OIDC_TOKEN=$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \

          if [ -z "$OIDC_TOKEN" ] || [ "$OIDC_TOKEN" = "null" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to retrieve Snowflake OIDC token"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Debug: show token claims (sub, aud, iss) without exposing the full token
          echo "$OIDC_TOKEN" | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d 2>/dev/null | jq '{sub, aud, iss}' || true
          echo "::add-mask::$OIDC_TOKEN"
          echo "SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN=$OIDC_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Login to R2 backend
        run: pulumi login 's3://pulumi?endpoint=https://${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com&region=auto&s3ForcePathStyle=true'

      - name: Select stack
        run: pulumi stack select dev

      - name: Pulumi Preview
        id: preview
        run: |
          set +e

          # Run preview with JSON output for parsing
          pulumi preview --json 2>/dev/null > preview.json
          JSON_EXIT=$?

          # Also get human-readable output
          pulumi preview --diff 2>&1 | tee preview.txt
          PREVIEW_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

          echo "exit_code=$PREVIEW_EXIT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Parse JSON for accurate counts
          if [ -f preview.json ] && [ -s preview.json ]; then
            CREATES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "create")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            UPDATES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "update")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            DELETES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "delete")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")

            UPDATES=$(grep -c "^\s*~.*update" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")

          echo "deletes=$DELETES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-no%20changes-green?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"

          cat << 'COMMENT_EOF' > comment.md

          <summary>📋 Preview Details</summary>


          ---

          END_EOF

          # Replace placeholders
          sed -i "s|HEADER_PLACEHOLDER|$HEADER|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|BADGE_PLACEHOLDER|$BADGE|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|CREATES_PLACEHOLDER|$CREATES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|UPDATES_PLACEHOLDER|$UPDATES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|DELETES_PLACEHOLDER|$DELETES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|SAMES_PLACEHOLDER|$SAMES|g" comment.md

      - name: Post PR Comment
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const body = fs.readFileSync('infrastructure/pulumi/comment.md', 'utf8');

            const marker = '<!-- pulumi-preview-comment -->';
            const fullBody = marker + '\n' + body;

            // Find existing comment
            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existingComment = comments.find(c => c.body.includes(marker));

            if (existingComment) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existingComment.id,
                body: fullBody
              });
              console.log('Updated existing comment');
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body: fullBody
              });
              console.log('Created new comment');
            }

      - name: Set exit code
        if: steps.preview.outputs.result == 'failed'
        run: exit 1

name: Pulumi Preview

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "infrastructure/pulumi/**"
      - ".github/workflows/pulumi-preview.yml"

env:
  CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
  CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
  AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
  PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE }}
  SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ secrets.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
  SNOWFLAKE_USER: PULUMI_SVC
  SNOWFLAKE_AUTHENTICATOR: WORKLOAD_IDENTITY
  SNOWFLAKE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER: OIDC
  SNOWFLAKE_ROLE: PULUMI_ROLE

jobs:
  preview:
    name: Preview
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: pulumi
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: infrastructure/pulumi

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.24"
          cache-dependency-path: infrastructure/pulumi/go.sum

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: go mod tidy

      - name: Get Snowflake OIDC token
        run: |
          OIDC_TOKEN=$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
            "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=https://${SNOWFLAKE_ORGANIZATION_NAME}-${SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_NAME}.snowflakecomputing.com" | jq -r '.value')
          if [ -z "$OIDC_TOKEN" ] || [ "$OIDC_TOKEN" = "null" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to retrieve Snowflake OIDC token"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Debug: show token claims (sub, aud, iss) without exposing the full token
          echo "$OIDC_TOKEN" | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d 2>/dev/null | jq '{sub, aud, iss}' || true
          echo "::add-mask::$OIDC_TOKEN"
          echo "SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN=$OIDC_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Login to R2 backend
        run: pulumi login 's3://pulumi?endpoint=https://${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com&region=auto&s3ForcePathStyle=true'

      - name: Select stack
        run: pulumi stack select dev

      - name: Pulumi Preview
        id: preview
        run: |
          set +e

          # Run preview with JSON output for parsing
          pulumi preview --json 2>/dev/null > preview.json
          JSON_EXIT=$?

          # Also get human-readable output
          pulumi preview --diff 2>&1 | tee preview.txt
          PREVIEW_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

          echo "exit_code=$PREVIEW_EXIT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Parse JSON for accurate counts
          if [ -f preview.json ] && [ -s preview.json ]; then
            CREATES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "create")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            UPDATES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "update")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            DELETES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "delete")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            SAMES=$(jq '[.steps[]? | select(.op == "same")] | length' preview.json 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
          else
            # Fallback to text parsing
            CREATES=$(grep -c "^\s*+.*create" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            UPDATES=$(grep -c "^\s*~.*update" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            DELETES=$(grep -c "^\s*-.*delete" preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
            SAMES=$(grep -oP '\d+(?= unchanged)' preview.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
          fi

          echo "creates=$CREATES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "updates=$UPDATES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "deletes=$DELETES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "sames=$SAMES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Determine result status
          TOTAL_CHANGES=$((CREATES + UPDATES + DELETES))
          if [ $PREVIEW_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "result=failed" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          elif [ $TOTAL_CHANGES -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "result=no-changes" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "result=has-changes" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Generate PR Comment
        id: comment
        run: |
          RESULT="${{ steps.preview.outputs.result }}"
          CREATES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.creates }}"
          UPDATES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.updates }}"
          DELETES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.deletes }}"
          SAMES="${{ steps.preview.outputs.sames }}"

          # Set header based on result
          case $RESULT in
            "failed")
              HEADER="## ❌ Pulumi Preview Failed"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-failed-red?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
            "no-changes")
              HEADER="## ✅ Pulumi Preview: No Changes"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-no%20changes-green?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
            "has-changes")
              HEADER="## 🔄 Pulumi Preview: Changes Detected"
              BADGE="https://img.shields.io/badge/pulumi-changes%20detected-blue?style=flat-square&logo=pulumi"
              ;;
          esac

          # Build comment
          cat << 'COMMENT_EOF' > comment.md
          HEADER_PLACEHOLDER

          ![Pulumi](BADGE_PLACEHOLDER)

          ### 📊 Resource Changes

          | | Create | Update | Delete | Unchanged |
          |:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
          | Count | **CREATES_PLACEHOLDER** | **UPDATES_PLACEHOLDER** | **DELETES_PLACEHOLDER** | SAMES_PLACEHOLDER |
          | | 🆕 | 📝 | 🗑️ | ⏸️ |

          COMMENT_EOF

          # Add warning section for destructive changes
          if [ "$DELETES" -gt 0 ]; then
            cat << 'WARNING_EOF' >> comment.md

          > [!CAUTION]
          > **DELETES_PLACEHOLDER resources will be deleted.** Please review carefully before merging.

          WARNING_EOF
          fi

          # Add details section
          cat << 'DETAILS_EOF' >> comment.md

          <details>
          <summary>📋 Preview Details</summary>

          ```diff
          DETAILS_EOF

          # Add preview output (truncated if needed)
          head -c 60000 preview.txt >> comment.md

          cat << 'END_EOF' >> comment.md
          ```

          </details>

          ---

          <sub>🏗️ **Stack:** `dev` | 📁 **Path:** `infrastructure/pulumi` | 🔗 **Workflow:** [Run #${{ github.run_number }}](${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }})</sub>
          END_EOF

          # Replace placeholders
          sed -i "s|HEADER_PLACEHOLDER|$HEADER|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|BADGE_PLACEHOLDER|$BADGE|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|CREATES_PLACEHOLDER|$CREATES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|UPDATES_PLACEHOLDER|$UPDATES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|DELETES_PLACEHOLDER|$DELETES|g" comment.md
          sed -i "s|SAMES_PLACEHOLDER|$SAMES|g" comment.md

      - name: Post PR Comment
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const body = fs.readFileSync('infrastructure/pulumi/comment.md', 'utf8');

            const marker = '<!-- pulumi-preview-comment -->';
            const fullBody = marker + '\n' + body;

            // Find existing comment
            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existingComment = comments.find(c => c.body.includes(marker));

            if (existingComment) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existingComment.id,
                body: fullBody
              });
              console.log('Updated existing comment');
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body: fullBody
              });
              console.log('Created new comment');
            }

      - name: Set exit code
        if: steps.preview.outputs.result == 'failed'
        run: exit 1

エラーメッセージが変わりました！今度はより具体的です：

```
JWT contains an invalid audience ('aud') claim.
The JWT's audience is [https://***-***.snowflakecomputing.com],
but it must be a non-empty subset of the audience list [snowflakecomputing.com].
```

**原因**: Snowflake が期待する audience は `snowflakecomputing.com` なのに、トークンの audience は `https://<org>-<account>.snowflakecomputing.com` になっています。

2箇所を修正する必要があります：

1. **ワークフロー**: OIDC トークン取得時の audience を `snowflakecomputing.com` に変更
2. **または bootstrap.sql**: `OIDC_AUDIENCE_LIST` でフルURLを許可

シンプルな方法（ワークフロー側で audience を合わせる）で修正します。
